writeup.p: The server's answer to C14PacketTabComplete: a VarInt count followed by the matching command and player-name strings. The vanilla GUI feeds them into GuiChat.onAutocompleteResponse to cycle suggestions on Tab. Because Bukkit forks populate the server command registry from plugins, the response leaks plugin names as colon-prefixed commands (/plugin:subcommand), which is the entire basis of the plugin-enumeration features in the corpus.

NetHandlerPlayServer.processTabComplete asks the command dispatcher for matches and echoes them back as S3APacketTabComplete with no rate limit and no length guard beyond the request's own string cap. Client side, handleTabComplete dispatches on the main thread and, only when the current screen is a GuiChat, calls onAutocompleteResponse; any other screen means the payload is silently ignored, a detail modules must remember when they fire requests outside chat.

Three corpus features. Rise 5.99 Plugins sends C14 with '/' in Normal mode or '/a' through '/z' in Bypass mode, then parses every S3A response, splits on ':' and filters '/minecraft' to print the plugin list; Bypass defers the printout to onDisable. Sigma 4.11 PluginFinder is a command doing the same with a 20-second listen window, its own dedupe and a cancel of the event. Rise 6.1.30 and 6.2.4 Chat reimplements the chat screen and consumes S3A for autocomplete cycling: it stores the matches on receive, rotates through them on Tab, and fires C14 itself with the typed text and an optional targeted BlockPos.

The enumeration trick is the exploit: a server that does not filter tab completion inventories its own plugins, which names the anti-cheat and its version for targeted research. Bypass modes blast up to 26 requests in one burst, which is a clean rate signal; servers that rate-limit C14 or strip plugin-prefixed commands from the registry kill both modes. The GUI dependency is the subtle constraint: S3A only reaches the vanilla autocomplete when a chat screen is open, so UI-less requesters must hold their own state.

overview: The tab-completion response channel and the backbone of plugin enumeration: Bukkit leaks plugin names as colon-prefixed commands. Three corpus features consume it: Rise 5.99 Plugins (Normal and Bypass modes), Sigma 4.11's PluginFinder command, and the Rise 6.x Chat module, which uses S3A for its autocomplete cycling.
server_handling: processTabComplete resolves matches from the server command registry and player list, then sends S3A. There is no server-side rate limit in vanilla; rate limiting lives in plugins. The response is a snapshot, one S3A per request in order, and nothing invalidates a previous response, which is why burst enumeration is reliable.
protocol_notes: VarInt count, then count strings, each VarInt-length-prefixed UTF-8, bounded by the 32767-byte frame limit per string. The request may carry an optional targeted BlockPos that enables coordinate-aware completions, but the response carries no position data back. Results arrive in registry order, which is why cycling modules rotate through the array instead of assuming alphabetical order.
anticheat_landscape: Anti-cheats do not flag S3A; they flag the request side. A burst of 26 C14 packets inside one tick is a clean rate signal, which makes Rise 5.99's Normal mode (one request, one parse) the safe variant and Bypass the risky one. Servers defeat enumeration server-side by filtering S3A responses or hiding plugin-prefixed commands, both invisible to the client.

modules.name: Plugins
modules.purpose: Enumerate server plugins by parsing the colon-prefixed commands leaked in tab-completion responses.
modules.how_it_works: Normal mode sends one C14PacketTabComplete("/") on enable and parses the S3A response immediately, splitting each command on ':' and filtering the '/minecraft' namespace; results print to chat as they arrive and the module toggles off. Bypass mode fires 26 requests ('/a' through '/z') and defers the deduped printout to onDisable. Timeouts (5s Normal, 2.5s Bypass) disable the module when the server returns nothing.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Normal mode is low-risk: one request, one parse. Bypass mode fires 26 C14 packets back to back, a clean rate signal for servers that rate-limit tab completion; the responses themselves are never flagged.
modules.variations: Sigma 4.11 implements the same idea as the PluginFinder command; Rise 6.x moved the mechanics into the Chat module's autocomplete.

modules.name: Chat
modules.purpose: Replacement chat screen with custom autocomplete: S3A responses feed the Tab cycling and the module sends C14 requests itself.
modules.how_it_works: On PacketReceiveEvent, every S3A is stored into a matches list and each match is printed to chat. On the Tab key, if matches is empty the module sends C14PacketTabComplete with the typed text and an optional targeted BlockPos (the looked-at block), then cycles the stored matches on subsequent Tab presses. The dot-prefix guard skips requests for client command input, and the matches list is nulled when the input closes.
modules.vanilla_hook: PacketReceiveEvent (S3A storage), GuiKeyBoardEvent (Tab cycling and C14 send).
modules.anti_cheat_notes: No anti-cheat surface; the module is a UI replacement. The C14 traffic it generates is identical to vanilla autocomplete traffic.
modules.variations: Rise 6.1.30 ships the same module under com/alan/clients/module/impl/render/chat with an identical S3A branch.

modules.name: PluginFinder (command)
modules.purpose: Command-driven plugin enumeration: send one C14 for '/', listen for a single S3A, print the deduped plugin list.
modules.how_it_works: fire() resets a timer, registers the command object with the event system and sends C14PacketTabComplete("/"). The event handler waits for S3A, splits each command on ':', dedupes plugin names, filters 'minecraft' and 'bukkit', prints the list, unregisters and cancels the event. A 20-second timer self-unregisters if the server never answers.
modules.vanilla_hook: EventPacket via a self-registered command listener; C14 sent through NetUtil.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: A single C14 request is indistinguishable from vanilla autocomplete, making the command the stealthiest enumeration variant in the corpus.
modules.variations: Rise 5.99's Plugins module covers the same ground with Normal and Bypass modes; PluginFinder is the one-shot command form.

general_hooks: PacketReceiveEvent on every client; the request side is a raw C14 construction, and Sigma sends it through NetUtil while Rise uses PacketUtil.
client_variations: Rise 5.99 parses responses live and toggles off; Sigma registers and unregisters a one-shot listener; Rise 6.x keeps the matches as GUI state for Tab cycling. None of them rely on the vanilla GuiChat path, which is exactly what the vanilla handler requires.
